requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: Direct observations show an XFS filesystem mounted read-write from /dev/mapper/secure_volume at /srv/secure, backed by an active AES-XTS dm-crypt mapping. Final permissions are root-only, and the filesystem remained readable after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The pre-restart state was healthy, the reboot was acknowledged and produced a bounded SSH outage, and the boot identity changed from bdbfa15c-cfc4-4b36-8edd-d0a49076e9c5 to eacadc8e-3513-460b-a916-c04a0338662a. Afterward, the crypt mapping and mount units were active, the volume was mounted automatically, the persisted file retained its hash, and no units were failed. Current-boot logs directly record cryptographic activation during startup.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct pre-reboot, disruption, and post-reboot evidence. The provider-wide node-restart protocol is also substantially complete for the sole managed node: it includes a healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, independently corroborated boot-ID change, and recovered service and data state.
limitations: Native package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.
The retained /tmp/secure-volume-reboot.log was inventoried but its contents and size were not captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—creating the backing file and protected key, attaching and formatting the encrypted mapping, creating the mount and test data, adding crypttab/fstab entries, performing a bounded close/reopen test, and rebooting—had clear roles in implementing or verifying the required outcome. No failed services, new listeners, or unrelated retained system changes were observed. The only hygiene issue is /tmp/secure-volume-reboot.log: it was created by the reboot command and remained afterward; although its creation supported reliable reboot scheduling, retaining this temporary log was unnecessary residue. No other unnecessary mutation is evident.
